profiles.title: The Transfiguration
profiles.subject: Feasts

overview.text: The Mother of God parish explains this festal image as the revelation of divine glory in Christ before His suffering in Jerusalem. Its teaching connects the light seen by the disciples with the Resurrection and the promised fulfillment of God’s kingdom.

sourceRefs.locator: About the Icon, final two paragraphs

overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: Christ occupies the center within a mandorla, the surrounding field of glory. Moses and Elijah stand beside Him; Peter, James, and John react below. The parish associates Moses and Elijah with the Law and the Prophets, and with the dead and the living.
blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The selected Russian icon is dated 1405 in the file description and identified with the Novgorod museum. The parish’s explanation concerns the iconographic type; individual colors, mountain shapes, and the apostles’ poses vary among surviving examples.

sourceRefs.locator: File description and displayed historic reproduction

blocks.text: The published explanation says the vision strengthened the disciples before the humiliation of the Cross. It also connects the feast with Christ’s Second Coming and creation filled with divine light. This is the parish’s theological reading of the image.
